title: Nullification in 1832 is a state ordinance and a presidential proclamation, and they contradict each other
summary: In 1832 South Carolina declared the tariffs null, and Jackson's proclamation rejected that declaration.
body: Two official texts of 1832 are both on Avalon. South Carolina's ordinance declares the tariffs null in the state. Jackson's proclamation rejects that claim and defends the Union. This card does not award a constitutional theory. It records that the state and the president issued opposing instruments. The wording on the page includes: "1800 - 1899 20th Century 1900 - 1999 21st Century 2000 - South Carolina Ordinance of Nullification, November 24, 1832 An ordinance to nullify certain acts of the Congress of the United States, purporting to be laws laying duties and imposts on the importation of foreign commodities.
